children: Basis bids for corn shipped by barge to the U.S. Gulf Coast firmed on Tuesday and soybean bids eased, as the rally in the grain market continued and had some export buyers looking to South America for deals, traders said.
Strength in the U.S. dollar also weighed on export demand, as it makes already high-priced ag products more expensive for importers.

Soybeans and soymeal futures hit session highs after the National Oilseed Processors Association said its membership crushed 205.456 million bushels of soybeans in August, an 11-month low, and soyoil stocks thinned to the lowest level since November 2024.
A jump in crude oil prices
lent additional support to soybeans and corn futures on Tuesday, both of which are used in the production of biofuels.

Traders said they also remain optimistic about Chinese export demand for U.S. soy ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping's upcoming visit to Washington. China's total U.S. soybean buying has clocked in at nearly half of the 25 million tons the White House said Beijing had committed to annually through 2028.
Brazil soy exports are expected to reach 8.32 million metric tons in September, compared to the 7.74 million tons estimated in the previous week, ANEC reported on Tuesday.

CIF soybean barges loaded in October traded at 100 cents over CBOT November (SX26) futures, while November loadings traded at 114 cents and 115 cents over November futures and December loadings traded at 106 cents over CBOT January 2027 (SF27) futures.

Meanwhile, CIF soybean barges loaded in September were bid sharply lower, with bids at 85 cents over CBOT November (SX26) futures. October barges were bid at 98 cents over futures. Bids for November and December barges firmed slightly.
FOB export premiums for Gulf soybean shipments in October eased, offered at around 124 cents over November futures, while November shipments were offered at 127 cents over futures.
Bids for CIF corn barges were mixed, with September loadings bid higher at 74 cents over CBOT December (CZ26) futures, while October barge bids eased at 85 cents over December futures.

FOB export premiums for Gulf corn vessels loaded in the first half of October firmed slightly, offered at around 106 cents over December futures, while latter-half October were offered at 109 cents over December futures.
